shape.description: Green three-cell chute with tall flat side walls, straight in plan. From the high end it drops steeply, then runs out flat to the low end. A bridge across the walls at the bend carries an axle with a four-bladed curved orange paddle wheel that reaches down into the channel. Tongues at both ends, as on T-06. No legs: it hangs between two supports.
shape.sizeBasis: Length measured on reference/uploads/M-12_1793563400741.jpg against the light-blue blocks beside it: the chute, tongue to tongue, is about 2.5 block widths (about 115 mm at 45 mm a cell), its high end clipped to a block one slot above its low end. Width from the channel against a marble; height includes the paddle wheel. No ruler; +-10%.

physics.behaviour: A gravity slide. The marble rolls down and pushes through the orange paddles, which turn, and slows a little. Nothing adds energy.

evidence.source: lp_plans_04 step 3-4 and crop of lp_plans_15
evidence.shows: Placement 1: high end clips to the B-01 at z 2 of the front-left tower, under its B-04. Low end enters the flank of M-01.
Placement 2: high end on a B-01 at A3, low end on a B-03 at A6, spanning three cells. Dark red arrow points downhill along it. Measured drop about 1 slot.
An orange four-bladed paddle wheel lies loose in the pile.
Real piece: straight in plan, steep drop then a flat run-out, paddle wheel on a bridge at the bend

Chute about 2.5 block widths long overall; the old 190 mm came from a 62 mm cell estimate. A tall flat side panel over the steep part, a bracket over the bend carrying a four-bladed curved orange wheel, a flat run-out with lower walls ending in a hooked tongue.

assumptions: Origin at footprint centre at foot level (the top plane of whatever the piece stands on). East is +x, south is +y, z in slots.
The loose four-bladed wheel in the photos is assumed to be this piece's paddle.
Free rotation is inferred from the axle hub in the drawing.
Origin at the lowest seat because the piece has no foot.
openQuestions: Can a slow marble stall at the paddles?
Is the wheel really removable? Is it meant to come off?
